title: Half a signature
notes: The science: the graft. Morphogenic markers plus something the Doctor
cannot place -- he is reading half a signature (LORE.md 1b, entry four).

lines.text: INCOMING: U.S.S. ADIRONDACK. TWO VOICES
Shepard. I've got the Doctor with me. Ours.
Good afternoon. Or whatever it is on the surface.

options.text: Is this going to be bad news?

lines.text: INCOMING: U.S.S. ADIRONDACK. TWO VOICES
I did say they wouldn't pick up. I said it twice.
You did. Shuttle, have you got a moment?
Your shuttle's hologram has been sending me readings.
Sensibly formatted, which I did not expect from a
copy of myself. I suppose I should be flattered.
The crew you've sent up brought samples on their boots.
Accidentally. I have made the most of them.
The dead down there are not dead in the usual way.
Something rebuilt them. Morphogenic markers, yes,
the Founders' own chemistry, which is bad enough.
But there's a second signature underneath it.
Something is holding the tissue together. Running it.
Two different things did this. I can see one of them.
The other is only an outline. A gap in the data.
I don't know. I do so dislike saying that.
I can support the chemistry. I cannot support the author.
He keeps saying that. It still sounds like Section 31.
It sounds like whoever you have already decided on.

options.text: Who do you think it is?

lines.text: I think it is two people who never met. One made
the poison and one made the engine. Don't quote me.
It matters to me. It'll matter to whoever gets home.
It matters to a cure. Which is my department.
The living, if they're caught early? Your shuttle
does that already, at a price. The dead? No.
I'm sorry. I would like to be wrong about that.
Thank you, Doctor. Shuttle, Shepard out.
